name: LifeWire NullCrave Addiction Suppression Node
body_location: cranial — subdermal placement at the prefrontal-temporal junction, minimal-incision insertion
description:
The NullCrave is a prefrontal neuromodulation implant that targets the mesolimbic reward pathway — specifically, it monitors dopaminergic signaling patterns associated with craving states and delivers precisely timed transcranial micro-stimulation pulses to the prefrontal cortex that strengthen inhibitory control over reward-seeking behavior. The device does not suppress pleasure broadly or eliminate dopamine function; rather, it intervenes at the moment a craving pattern is neurologically detected — identified by its characteristic pre-conscious signal signature — and amplifies the brain's own regulatory response before the craving reaches conscious experience. Users describe the effect not as suppression but as simply not having the urge: the moment when a craving would have arisen passes without event. The NullCrave is calibrated to a specific substance or behavioral profile during a two-week neurological mapping period and can hold up to three concurrent addiction profiles, with additional profiles available via licensed clinical expansion.

Addiction in GLMZ is not a personal failing — it is a structural consequence of the city's tiers. The Shelf runs on cheap synthetic stimulants, sedatives, and inhalants that make unbearable conditions bearable, and the line between coping and dependency is crossed so routinely that it is barely a line at all. LifeWire positioned the NullCrave as a dignified exit — not a punishment, not a program, not a room full of strangers, but a quiet internal adjustment that gives the user back their own agency. The marketing is careful: LifeWire never calls it a cure, always a tool. In practice, users across all tiers — from Shelf residents trying to step back from synthetics to Tier 4 executives managing stimulant dependency from fifteen-hour workdays — describe it as the first thing that actually worked. It does not fix the conditions that created the addiction. That part, as every honest clinician in the city will tell you, is still on the person and the world around them.
installation_requirements: Licensed neurotechnician or clinical pharmacologist required; outpatient procedure under local anesthetic; 25-minute installation with two-week neurological calibration period; initial calibration requires three short clinic check-ins during the mapping window
maintenance: Firmware sync every 6 months; addiction profile recalibration available at any LifeWire clinic if substances or behavioral patterns change; battery is inductive, harvested from normal neural electrical activity; full hardware review every 4 years

side_effects: During the calibration period, users may experience heightened awareness of craving states as the device maps signal patterns before active suppression begins
Some users report a brief, mild emotional flatness in the first month as the reward pathway adjusts to modulated signaling — typically resolves within six weeks
Rare cases of mild headache and light sensitivity in the first week post-installation
A small percentage of users report unusually vivid dreams involving the substance or behavior being suppressed during the calibration window
cultural_context: The NullCrave is one of LifeWire's most culturally complex products. In the lower tiers, it carries a layered meaning: getting one can be an act of profound self-determination, but it can also be something that a family member, an employer, or a court order pushes someone toward — and the line between chosen treatment and coerced compliance is contested territory in GLMZ's labor and civil rights discourse. LifeWire has faced ongoing legal challenges over corporate wellness programs that effectively require employees to install NullCraves as a condition of health insurance coverage. In the Shelf, community attitudes are mixed: some see it as a genuine lifeline, others as a tool for making people more productive workers without addressing why they needed to cope in the first place. Among Tier 3 and 4 users, it tends to be discussed with the same frank pragmatism as any other health intervention — something you get because it works, and something you do not particularly advertise.

corporate employees in high-pressure Tier 3-4 roles managing stimulant dependency
people in recovery who want a neurological support layer alongside other treatment
individuals court-ordered into addiction management programs
story_hooks: A Tier 1 community organizer approaches the players with evidence that a local employer is offering NullCrave installations as a 'voluntary' benefit — but the devices are calibrated not just for substances but for a behavioral profile that includes the neurological signature of collective action and protest, which apparently shares enough signal overlap with compulsive craving that LifeWire's algorithm flags it.

A black-market NullCrave recalibration service has appeared on the Shelf — someone is offering to expand the device's suppression profiles beyond the licensed three-profile limit, but users who have had the modification are reporting that it is suppressing things they did not consent to suppress.

A player's contact went through a NullCrave installation six months ago and has been clean — but they have also stopped caring about things they used to care deeply about, and the flat affect is getting worse. Their device logs show the suppression is operating within normal parameters. Whatever is happening is not in the manual.
